svg.title: The billing boundary moves when the server stops asking the host for a model
svg.desc: Two panels drawn on the same grid, so the only difference between them is the one the post is about. The left panel, headed Then, shows sampling: a host that owns the model, a client below it, and a server below that, with two dashed red arrows running upward from the server through the client to the host, each struck out with a cross. One is labelled sampling/createMessage and the other says there is no back channel to carry it. A dashed box marked billing boundary encloses the host alone. A note records that the feature is deprecated with removal no earlier than 2027-07-28, but that the back channel it traveled over was deleted in this same revision with no window, and that the deletion is what breaks code. The right panel, headed Now, keeps the same three boxes at the same heights, but the arrows run downward and are live: the host calls the client, the client sends tools/call to the server, and the server reaches a model provider API over HTTPS, drawn in neither blue nor terracotta because it is outside MCP entirely. The identical dashed billing boundary has moved to enclose the server and the provider together. A three-row table underneath answers the questions the move changes: who pays goes from the host to the server operator, who consented goes from the user at the host's prompt to the operator at deploy time, and who answers for the prompt stays the server author in both columns.
svg.text: When the server needs a model of its own
The mechanism changed. So did who pays and who consented. Who answers for the prompt did not.
